questions.text: Walk me through an analysis that changed a real decision. What was the before and after?
questions.rationale: Impact-anchored storytelling separates decision-support analysts from report factories.

questions.text: Tell me about a time your analysis was wrong and someone acted on it. What happened next?
questions.rationale: Error ownership and correction behavior under real consequences.

questions.text: Describe your approach to validating a dataset you have never seen before.
questions.rationale: Data skepticism routines are the analyst's core craft.

questions.text: How do you explain confidence intervals to a stakeholder who just wants the number?
questions.rationale: Uncertainty communication is where analytics earns or loses trust.

questions.text: Tell me about a metric you built that the company still uses. Why did it stick?
questions.rationale: Durable metric design requires understanding both the business and the failure modes.

questions.text: Describe a time a stakeholder wanted data to support a decision they had already made. What did you do?
questions.rationale: The decision-based-evidence-making test; integrity under social pressure.

questions.text: Walk me through your SQL habits. What does your query look like just before you share results?
questions.rationale: Verification habits at the query level predict output reliability.

questions.text: What kind of analytical problem makes you lose track of time?
questions.rationale: Genuine analytical curiosity, located specifically.

questions.text: Tell me about the messiest data environment you have worked in. How did you stay productive?
questions.rationale: Real environments are messy; coping strategy beats tool wishlists.

questions.text: Describe an A/B test you designed. What did you get wrong in the design and catch later?
questions.rationale: Experimental design maturity, evidenced through self-caught flaws.

questions.text: How do you decide between a quick answer now and a rigorous answer next week? Give an example of each.
questions.rationale: Speed-rigor calibration is the daily judgment call of applied analytics.

questions.text: Tell me about a dashboard you built that nobody used. Why not, and what did you do about it?
questions.rationale: The unused-dashboard story tests user empathy and follow-through over shipping.

questions.text: Walk me through how you would investigate a sudden 20 percent drop in a key metric.
questions.rationale: Decomposition method under ambiguity; the classic diagnostic scenario.

questions.text: Describe your experience with data modeling. Tell me about a schema or semantic layer choice you defended.
questions.rationale: Modeling opinions with reasons indicate depth beyond query writing.

questions.text: What is your relationship with statistics, honestly? Where does your knowledge get thin?
questions.rationale: Calibrated self-knowledge about statistical limits prevents overconfident analysis.

questions.text: Tell me about presenting analysis to executives. What did you cut from the deck, and why?
questions.rationale: Editorial judgment for senior audiences; the cutting decision is the skill.

questions.text: How do you document your analyses so someone can reproduce them in six months?
questions.rationale: Reproducibility hygiene, a fair early-career expectation.

questions.text: Describe a time you found something in the data nobody asked about. What did you do with it?
questions.rationale: Proactive curiosity paired with the judgment to escalate appropriately.

questions.text: Tell me about working with an engineer to fix a data pipeline. Who owned what?
questions.rationale: Analytics-engineering collaboration boundaries, tested through a real incident.

questions.text: What is the difference between an insight and an observation? Give me one of each from your last role.
questions.rationale: The distinction separates analysts who drive action from those who narrate data.

questions.text: How would you set up analytics from scratch at a company with no tracking? What is week one?
questions.rationale: Zero-to-one instrumentation instinct, a lead-level architecture question.

questions.text: Describe a time you had to tell a leader their favorite metric was misleading.
questions.rationale: Truth-to-power with statistical grounding; both halves need to be present.

questions.text: Tell me about mentoring someone in SQL or analysis. What did they struggle with and how did you help?
questions.rationale: Teaching ability evidences depth and multiplies team capability.

questions.text: What analytics work do you find tedious, and how do you make yourself do it well anyway?
questions.rationale: Honest relationship with the unglamorous majority of the job.

questions.text: Walk me through a time you used cohort analysis to answer a retention question. What did you find?
questions.rationale: Cohort fluency is a checkable, concrete method question.

questions.text: How do you handle a request queue longer than your week? What actually gets dropped?
questions.rationale: Prioritization under demand overload, the analyst's permanent condition.

questions.text: Describe your experience with a BI tool migration or evaluation. What criteria mattered most?
questions.rationale: Tool evaluation reveals whether the candidate thinks in workflows or feature lists.

questions.text: Tell me about a data quality issue you caught just before it went to the board or an investor.
questions.rationale: High-stakes verification instinct with a memorable story attached.

questions.text: As an analytics lead, how do you balance service work against foundational projects? What ratio do you defend?
questions.rationale: Portfolio management for analytics teams; the defended ratio shows conviction.

questions.text: What does responsible use of company data mean to you in practice, beyond the policy document?
questions.rationale: Data ethics as lived practice rather than compliance recitation.
